articles.title: 'No one can escape law': BJP as CBI registers FIR against Punjab CM’s OSD in corruption case
articles.description: New Delhi, Oct 10 (IANS) The BJP on Saturday said that no one could escape the law after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered an FIR against Rajbir Ghuman, Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, in a corruption case. Speaking to IANS, BJP leader Sunil Jakhar said, “I would only say, ‘Run, Ghuman, run!’ No matter how much you run, you cannot hide. The law is closing in on you, and there is not much time left." "Ghuman is just the tip of the iceberg. The Aam Aadmi Party leaders, who were driven out of Delhi, have taken it upon themselves to loot Punjab in an organised manner,” he alleged. Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon said, “It has come to everyone’s attention through the media that the CBI pasted a notice at his residence. Now, he says he has not received the notice. What can we make of this? He is contradicting himself and lying.” Custom Ad: Multiplex BJP leader Rana Gurmit Singh Sodhi said Ghuman should appear before the CBI and present his side of the case or offer any clarification through legal means. “He will have to do so sooner or later. How long can he keep running away? No one can escape the law. This behaviour suggests that he is guilty,” Sodhi said. BJP leader Amanjot Kaur Ramu Walia alleged that the Aam Aadmi Party was protesting to conceal its weaknesses. “If the Aam Aadmi Party has nothing to hide, why is it protesting? The CBI conducted a raid, and a notice was pasted outside the residence of the Chief Minister’s OSD. It is common knowledge among the public, including in villages, that money is being taken for transfers and that other money has also been collected,” she alleged. Meanwhile, the CBI has pasted the summons outside Ghuman’s residence in connection with allegations of bribery to influence government postings and administrative decisions. The agency registered an FIR against Ghuman and his associates following directions from the Punjab and Haryana High Court and a report from the Enforcement Directorate (ED). The move came after Ghuman failed to appear before the agency at its Chandigarh office on Wednesday for questioning. He had reportedly been asked to appear at 2.30 p.m. However, he did not attend, citing the absence of formal Service of Summons. In a press release, the CBI said it was investigating allegations of corruption involving the manipulation of IAS and IPS officers’ postings, departmental proceedings, policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions and licencing matters in exchange for financial benefits. --IANS jk/rad

articles.title: Maha govt sanctions Rs 12.68 crore for 44 VIP vehicles, including Rs 4.07 crore bulletproof Land Cruiser
articles.description: Amid seeking Central financial assistance to combat drought-like conditions across parts of the state, the Maharashtra government on Friday issued administrative approval to procure 44 new high-end vehicles worth Rs 12.68 crore for visiting dignitaries and VIPs. The fleet expansion includes a bulletproof Toyota Land Cruiser valued at Rs 4.07 crore. According to a Government Resolution (GR) issued by the Protocol Department, the new fleet will replace ageing vehicles to ensure seamless logistics and security for visiting dignitaries. The protocol branch handles transport arrangements for the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Union Ministers, Governors, Chief Ministers of other states, Supreme Court and High Court judges, and other high-level state guests. The sanctioned procurement will be carried out on a single-source basis through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal, following state financial and procurement regulations. The government has approved one bulletproof Toyota Land Cruiser at Rs 4,07,68,000, two Toyota Fortuners at Rs 30,00,000, one Urbania bus at Rs 31,00,000, 32 Toyota Innova Crystas at Rs 20,71,453, seven Maruti Ertigas at Rs 11,59,100, and one towing vehicle (as per government rates).The official order stipulates that all 44 vehicles must be sourced within the sanctioned budget of Rs 12,68,64,342. The funds will be disbursed through the Government Transport Service (GTS), Mumbai, and district collectorate protocol wings to complete the fleet upgrade without delay. The government's approval to procure 44 vehicles comes at a time when it is struggling to cope with drought-like conditions in 265 talukas. To support farmers, agricultural labourers, and affected rural populations, the state government has extended a 12-point relief and concessions package. The government is conducting panchnamas (assessments) and, thereafter, will decide on a financial relief package. The government has announced a full waiver of land revenue for affected farmers, restructuring of existing agricultural loans, an immediate stay on the recovery of all agriculture-related bank loans, exemption or concessions on current electricity bills for agricultural pumps above 7.5 HP capacity (up to 7.5 HP is already waived), waiver of examination fees for school and college students in the affected zones, relaxation of work-norm criteria under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act to maximise employment generation, and deployment of water tankers wherever drinking water shortages occur. Further, the government has issued strict orders preventing the disconnection of agricultural pump power supplies in declared scarcity villages, implementing targeted distribution systems to prevent foodgrain shortages for farmers and daily-wage agricultural workers, measures to ensure adequate supply and availability of fodder for cattle, immediate rollout of water conservation works in the affected belts, and comprehensive planning for drinking water and livestock water resources in accordance with government directives.
